task.description: Validate the CODE-DESIGNER Step 01 design for PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-03, PAR-04 (events table monthly range partitioning -- high risk, core table). Standard checks apply (every AC traced, no implementation code, tools/lint_design_artefact.py clean). CRITICAL ADDITIONAL CHECK: both PAR-01 and PAR-03 design docs flag that src/event_store/store.zig::Store.archive() currently issues DELETE FROM events / DELETE FROM events_archive-adjacent statements that become actively incompatible with PAR-03's own AC ("No DELETE statement SHALL run against events or events_archive at any point") the moment PAR-03 ships. Both docs recommend deferring archive()'s retirement/rewrite as a follow-up rather than fixing it in this batch, reasoning that PAR-01's ACs don't mention archive() and PAR-03's ACs govern the NEW retention mechanism, not the old one. Assess this reasoning carefully: does PAR-03's AC ("No DELETE... at any point") actually mean literally zero DELETE statements can exist in the codebase touching these tables once PAR-03 ships (in which case archive() being left as-is would make this batch's own release FALSELY claim AC compliance, since archive() would still be callable and would still violate it), or does it mean PAR-03's OWN mechanism specifically never deletes (a narrower, correct-as-designed reading)? This determines whether deferring archive() is safe or is a hidden AC violation. If genuinely ambiguous, this may need to route to REQ-ANALYST rather than being decided unilaterally by either CODE-DESIGNER or you.
acceptance_criteria: Every AC in PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-03, PAR-04 traced to a design section
No implementation code in the design
Migration approach correctly scoped as fresh-schema-only (not attempting PAR-05's online conversion)
Current events/events_archive shape preservation verified against actual migration history

Store.archive() vs PAR-03 DELETE-prohibition conflict explicitly resolved: either confirmed genuinely non-blocking with sound reasoning, or flagged as requiring REQ-ANALYST clarification before BACKEND-DEV proceeds

result.summary: Validated PAR-01..PAR-04 design artefacts (4 src/design/*.md + 2 templates/specs/*.yaml). All 6 artefacts pass tools/lint_design_artefact.py clean; both Type C YAMLs pass tools/codegen_migration.py --dry-run with previews covering their ACs. Migration scoping is correctly fresh-schema-only (PAR-01 explicitly excludes PAR-05's online conversion, guards with a zero-row check, raises rather than destroying data on a populated table). Current events/events_archive shape verified accurate against 001_event_store.sql, 003_event_archive.sql, 027_adp01_event_store_tenant.sql (columns, indexes, tenant_id addition all match). Migration numbers 1147-1149 correctly follow the actual latest (1146_ord04_plat_correlation_cursor.sql). FAIL for two reasons. (1) COVERAGE GAP (BLOCKER): PAR-03 AC1 ('RetentionClassForbidden rejects delete retention_class for protected-family event types INSTANCE_*/TASK_*/GATEWAY_*/EXECUTION_*') has no corresponding design element anywhere in par-03-partition-scoped-retention.md -- no function signature, no error taxonomy entry, no validation call site, no config/admin route. The design attributes this to ADP-11 (line 65, and the Zig comment near line 196), but grep confirms RetentionClassForbidden does not exist anywhere in src/ or tests/, and ADP-11 (already RELEASED per docs/requirements.yaml) predates the retention_class column this same PAR-03 migration creates -- ADP-11 cannot already validate a column that does not yet exist. The retention_class CHECK constraint the design does add only constrains the enum values (retain_forever/archive_queryable/delete); it has no awareness of event-type-name prefix, so it cannot by itself enforce AC1's protected-family rule. This is also a Security-checklist gap: because the config surface that sets retention_class is never designed, its input validation is also never specified. (2) ARCHIVE()/PAR-03 AMBIGUITY NEEDS REQ-ANALYST CLARIFICATION: PAR-03's body states 'No DELETE statement SHALL run against events or events_archive at any point' -- this sentence names the tables directly (not 'this mechanism') and adds 'at any point' with no mechanism-scoping qualifier, unlike PAR-01's own AC2 which DOES scope itself explicitly ('partitioning does not narrow idempotency to per-month scope') when a local-vs-global distinction is intended. A literalist reading supports 'zero DELETE statements against these tables anywhere in the codebase, full stop' -- not merely 'PAR-03's own new mechanism avoids DELETE'. None of PAR-03's six formal ACs restate this as a testable GIVEN/WHEN/THEN, so the constraint is a narrative design principle with no corresponding acceptance test. Both PAR-01's and PAR-03's designs correctly IDENTIFY that Store.archive() (src/event_store/store.zig:947, the ES-07 retention function, not the unrelated definition.Store.archive() workflow-status function) issues 'DELETE FROM events'/'DELETE FROM events_archive'-adjacent statements incompatible with a literal reading of this rule -- but both PRE-DECIDE the ambiguity unilaterally ('PAR-03's AC governs its own mechanism, not archive()') and recommend deferring archive()'s retirement, rather than routing the genuinely ambiguous text for clarification as the checklist requires ('if a requirement is ambiguous, flag it as an open question -- not guessed at'). CALL-SITE FINDING (verified by grep, not assumed): event_store.Store.archive() has ZERO call sites in src/ -- only in tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig. main.zig initializes event_store.Store (ev_store) but never calls .archive() on it. The three live 'store.archive(allocator, id)' call sites in src/api/routes/definitions.zig all resolve to the unrelated definition.Store.archive() (src/definition/store.zig:833, error.DefinitionNotFound/InvalidStatusTransition typed, a workflow-definition ACTIVE/DEPRECATED->ARCHIVED status transition with no events/events_archive interaction at all). So event_store.Store.archive() is dead code in production today -- this lowers practical urgency (no live request path currently violates the AC) but does NOT resolve whether the codebase, once compiled and shipped with this batch, would still technically violate a literally-read AC via a reachable-but-uncalled function. Given the genuine textual ambiguity and that resolving it wrong ships either an unnecessary blocker or a hidden compliance gap, this must route to REQ-ANALYST/ORCH for clarification of PAR-03's DELETE-prohibition scope, not be decided by CODE-DESIGNER or this validator.

issues.description: PAR-03 AC1 (RetentionClassForbidden guard rejecting delete retention_class for protected-family event types) has no design element: no function, no error taxonomy entry, no validation call site, no config/admin route in src/design/par-03-partition-scoped-retention.md. Falsely attributed to ADP-11, which is already-released and predates the retention_class column PAR-03 itself creates. CODE-DESIGNER must add: (a) the call site (likely Registry.registerType() or a new admin config-update path) that checks event_type prefix against {INSTANCE_*, TASK_*, GATEWAY_*, EXECUTION_*} before permitting retention_class = 'delete', (b) a RetentionClassForbidden error taxonomy entry, (c) validation-rule/access-control specification for whatever surface sets retention_class, since that is user input per the Security checklist.

PAR-03's body text 'No DELETE statement SHALL run against events or events_archive at any point' is genuinely ambiguous between (a) an absolute, codebase-wide prohibition on any DELETE against these two tables from any code path, and (b) a narrower statement that PAR-03's own new retention mechanism never issues DELETE. Both PAR-01's and PAR-03's designs identify that event_store.Store.archive() (src/event_store/store.zig:947) issues DELETE statements against events/events_archive and becomes incompatible with reading (a) the moment this batch ships, then unilaterally resolve the ambiguity toward reading (b) and recommend deferring archive()'s retirement as a later follow-up. Per this checklist's correctness criterion ('if ambiguous, flag as open question, do not guess'), this must route to REQ-ANALYST/ORCH for clarification before BACKEND-DEV proceeds, since guessing wrong ships a hidden compliance gap under this batch's own PAR-03 release claim. Mitigating context verified by grep: event_store.Store.archive() has zero call sites in src/ (only in tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig); it is not wired into main.zig or any live request path, so no CURRENT production behavior violates the AC even under reading (a) -- but the function remains compiled and callable, so the codebase-level compliance question is unresolved either way.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework (PAR-03 only): add RetentionClassForbidden design coverage for AC1, and either (a) get REQ-ANALYST/ORCH clarification on PAR-03's DELETE-prohibition scope and incorporate the answer, or (b) if clarification is not obtained before rework, design defensively to the literal/stricter reading (schedule archive()'s retirement/gating explicitly within this batch or as an immediately-following mandatory follow-up with a tracked issue, rather than an open question). PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-04 have no blocking issues of their own and may proceed once PAR-03 is reworked, but ORCH should confirm whether to hold all four together (they share migration numbering and cross-references) or split PAR-01/02/04 forward independently.
